claim: Israel is uniquely illegitimate because it was created through war and displacement.

heard.who: Ilan Pappé, historian, on the Verso Books blog (2018)
heard.quote: The crime committed by the leadership of the Zionist movement, which became the government of Israel, was that of ethnic cleansing.

answer: The 1940s were an age of mass transfers. The partition of India in 1947 displaced about 14 to 15 million people, with estimates of the dead from 200,000 to 2 million. About 12 to 14 million Germans were expelled or fled from eastern and central Europe, and estimates of their dead run from about 500,000 to 2 million. The Potsdam Agreement itself approved transfers, asking only that they be "orderly and humane". Poland's border moved west with them. Next to these, about 700,000 Palestinian Arabs left or were driven out in 1948, and some 850,000 Jews left Arab countries. This tells you the period, not who was right: these numbers are not a ranking of suffering, and they do not make any single act just.

contested: German expulsion deaths: the figure of about 2 million (West German government studies of the 1950s, by population balance) is disputed. Military historian Rüdiger Overmans counts about 500,000 deaths that are documented or plausible, and calls the remainder unexplained cases that need research.

1947 partition deaths: sources give 200,000 to one million (BBC), at least one million (The Guardian) and about one million (The Indian Express); Britannica gives 200,000 to 2 million. No census of the dead exists.

1948 Palestinian exodus: scholars agree on about 700,000 but disagree on cause. Benny Morris finds war, fear and expulsions in some places and no master plan; Ilan Pappé argues a planned ethnic cleansing; Efraim Karsh stresses Arab leaders' role. Card era3-exodus-causes-1948 holds that evidence.

Jews from Arab countries: the figure of about 850,000 is repeated by Jewish organisations and some news reports; Encyclopedia.com gives about 800,000. Scholars such as Yehouda Shenhav debate whether to call the departures a refugee flight (see card era3-jewish-refugees-arab-countries).

Whether these cases are a fair comparison is itself argued: a participant in the Israel Law Review discussion said the Sudeten expulsion was a punishment for the losers carried out under a peace agreement, which was not the case in 1948. Benny Morris replied that he cited it to show how the world judged such transfers at the time, not to justify them.
could_not_verify: Three readable reliable sources for the number of Poles moved out of former eastern Poland. The Polish government figure (3.5 million settled in the west, most from east of the Curzon Line) is in a US government document only. A scholar's count (Kochanowski: 1,503,263 Poles moved in 1944 to 1948 and about 518,000 Ukrainians, Belarusians and Lithuanians the other way) is in a PDF the checker cannot read.
The UNHCR page for the 14 million figure for the 1947 partition could not be read by the checker (it is a PDF); the figure is cited through Britannica, the BBC, Stanford and The Indian Express.
The UN Conciliation Commission's own 1949 estimate of 711,000 refugees could not be read on a page the checker can open; it is cited through the Israel Law Review and MERIP.
A scholarly source for the Jews who left Arab countries with a total count that the checker can read; Oxford and Buffalo Law pages were unreadable or showed only an abstract.
not_claimed: That because others did it, it was right. The card says what happened and how many, and the third card of this chapter says what the law was and is.
That any of these events were of equal size, cause or character; the numbers are set side by side and are not a ranking of suffering.
That the figures are exact. Most are estimates, and their sources are named.
That Israel's creation and the 1948 displacement were the same as the Potsdam transfers; the Allies agreed to the German transfers, and the Palestinian exodus had no such agreement.
